card.title: SHIFTING DOCTRINE
card.text: Shuffle a random card in hand into your deck, then draw 2 cards.
card.flavorText: As Allied forces reversed Japan’s early wartime gains, Japanese military strategy shifted dramatically after 1942. Following defeats at Midway and Guadalcanal, Japan abandoned offensive campaigns and adopted defensive attrition tactics, fortifying islands like Saipan and Iwo Jima to inflict heavy casualties. The desperate introduction of kamikaze attacks during the Battle of Leyte Gulf marked a turn to sacrificial warfare. On land, mobile tactics were replaced by last-stand defenses, with troops dug into caves, tunnels, and bunkers instead of fighting in open terrain. At sea, Japan resorted to decoy fleets, midget submarines, and asymmetric tactics as its navy weakened. Leaders like General Tadamichi Kuribayashi exemplified this approach where his defense of Iwo Jima focused on maximizing US losses rather than holding ground. The strategy no longer aimed for victory but tried to stall the American advance and pressure the Allies into a negotiated peace.
